findings.summary: The Everyday Commands section shows four commands with no line first saying what they do.
findings.evidence:
3. Everyday Commands
bash
aws s3 cp file s3://bucket/key
aws s3 ls s3://bucket/prefix/
findings.fix: Add a one-line idea before the code block, e.g. 'cp uploads, ls lists, sync mirrors a folder, rm deletes by prefix'. Or put a short comment above each command.

findings.summary: The blanket claim that archived objects need a restore before GET is wrong for Glacier Instant Retrieval, which serves reads in milliseconds.
findings.evidence: "Archived objects need a restore before GET" appears directly under a table where Glacier Instant is listed with "Get: ms". Page 1 and page 6 repeat the same line next to "Glacier Instant / Flexible".
findings.fix: Say "Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive objects need a restore before GET; Glacier Instant Retrieval is read directly in milliseconds." Make the same change on pages 1 and 6.

findings.summary: The Deep Archive retrieval times '~12h / ~48h' are never labeled as Standard and Bulk, so a learner cannot tell which tier each number belongs to.
findings.fix: Write 'Standard ~12h / Bulk ~48h' in the Get column, and give the Flexible tiers rough times (Expedited minutes, Standard hours, Bulk longer) so the Expedited/Standard/Bulk list has meaning.

findings.summary: NoncurrentVersionExpiration and 'old versions' are used before versioning, current versus noncurrent, and delete markers are introduced on page 4.
findings.evidence: Also set AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload, NoncurrentVersionExpiration ... Old versions? Expire noncurrent versions
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss on page 3, e.g. 'noncurrent = an older version kept after an overwrite or delete (see Versioning)', or move that rule to page 4.

findings.summary: The Get column and the retrieval tiers are shown without saying what they mean, so the '~12h / ~48h' values can't be read.
findings.evidence: Deep Archive | archive | 180d | ~12h / ~48h ... Flexible: Expedited, Standard, Bulk
findings.fix: Rename the column to 'Retrieval time'. Label the Deep Archive values (Standard ~12h, Bulk ~48h). Give a speed for each Flexible tier or drop the tier list.

findings.summary: The code block comes before its one-line explanation, and the explanation line is orphaned after it.
findings.evidence:
aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket b --prefix key
lists versions and delete markers
findings.fix: State the idea first ('Enable versioning, then list versions and delete markers'). Then show the two commands, with a comment on each one.

findings.summary: The Block Public Access bullet packs four separate switches into one line, and the ARN failure bullet is cryptic.
findings.evidence: Four switches: block public ACLs, ignore public ACLs, block public policies, restrict public buckets; One ARN form only gives AccessDenied for the other
findings.fix: Show the four switches as a short 2-column list or table of switch and what it does. Reword the ARN bullet to 'Wrong ARN form → AccessDenied (bucket ARN for object actions, or bucket/* for bucket actions)'.

findings.summary: The 'Classes and Versioning' section mixes three topics (classes, versioning, lifecycle), and one bullet holds three ideas.
findings.evidence: 2. Classes and Versioning ... Versioning: suspend only, never removed ... Lifecycle: expire noncurrent, abort incomplete multipart; Flat keys; strong read-after-write; last writer wins
findings.fix: Split into separate sections for Classes, Versioning and Lifecycle. Put each of 'flat keys', 'strong read-after-write' and 'last writer wins' on its own line.
